niche_preference_profile: This user most often prefers interfaces that feel clean, structured, and easy to scan: light or neutral backgrounds are common, spacing is usually more open, hierarchy is explicit, and controls are clearly emphasized without excessive clutter. They repeatedly favor rounded cards/buttons, clear grouped containers, visible labels, and layouts that separate sections cleanly. They also often like restrained but noticeable accent color—especially purple or warm accents—when it strengthens the primary action, though in some dense data views they prefer muted accents over overly saturated controls. Overall, they lean toward polished, modern, rounded, scan-friendly UI with strong clarity and moderate visual softness.

top_7_criteria.description: Prefers strong, explicit hierarchy with clear titles, subtitles, labels, section headings, selected states, and scan-friendly grouping.
Prefers more whitespace, open spacing, separated list items/cards, and less cramped vertical stacking.
Usually prefers light or neutral backgrounds with dark text and softer contrast over dark, heavy, or high-contrast themes.
Prefers a clearly dominant CTA or completion action with strong visibility and unambiguous action flow rather than split or weak emphasis.
Prefers softer rounded corners, pill buttons, and gentle card shapes rather than sharper or harsher component geometry.
Prefers content organized into clear cards, panels, rows, or modal-like containers with visible boundaries, separators, and grouping.
Prefers simpler layouts with fewer decorative elements, shorter copy, less promotional noise, and only essential controls visible.
